entries.claim: The average treatment effect is the expectation of the difference between the treated and untreated potential outcomes; the observed difference equals ATT plus selection bias when treatment is not randomised
entries.locator: Angrist & Pischke, Mostly Harmless Econometrics, Chapter 3 (potential outcomes)

entries.claim: The propensity score e(X)=P(T=1|X) balances the distribution of X across treatment groups, so conditioning on e(X) suffices when treatment assignment is conditionally ignorable
entries.notes: Basis of the propensity score definition and figure 2

entries.claim: The difference-in-differences estimator computes (treated pre-post change) minus (control pre-post change) and identifies the effect under the parallel trends assumption
entries.locator: Card & Krueger (1994), American Economic Review, minimum wage natural experiment

entries.claim: Regression discontinuity identifies a local effect as the jump in the outcome at the cutoff, assuming units cannot precisely manipulate the running variable
entries.locator: Lee & Lemieux (2010), Journal of Economic Literature 48(2), 281-355
entries.notes: Basis of equation 5 and the RDD section

entries.claim: An instrumental variable identifies a local average treatment effect for compliers when it is relevant (correlated with treatment) and exogenous (affects the outcome only through treatment)
entries.locator: Angrist & Pischke, Mostly Harmless Econometrics, Chapter 4 (instrumental variables)
entries.notes: Supports the IV portion of section 05

entries.claim: David Card, Joshua Angrist and Guido Imbens received the 2021 Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences for their contributions to the methodology of causal inference and natural experiments
entries.locator: The Nobel Prize, economic sciences 2021 summary

entries.claim: The four-method map, the overlap panels, and the DID example with values 100/115 and 95/100 are constructed teaching illustrations
entries.notes: Not results from any real study

entries.claim: The method-comparison map, the propensity-score overlap diagram and the parallel-trends diagram are schematic figures prepared for this lesson
entries.notes: Schematic; shapes and values illustrative only
